en.title: Minimum USB Drive Capacity for Distributing Games
en.description:
Distribute all n games among k children; each child must receive 1 or 2 games. Every child uses a USB drive of the same capacity. Find the minimum capacity.

The standard input format, examples and test data were written independently by CSWork.
en.input: The first line contains n k (1≤k≤n≤200000 and n≤2k); the second line contains the n game sizes (1..10⁹).
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer required by the problem.
en.explanation: Example 1: put 2 and 4 together and hand out 6 and 9 individually; the three USB drives hold 6, 6 and 9, so capacity 9 is enough, and it cannot be smaller than the size of game 9. Example 2: there is only one child, who must take both games, total size 3. Example 3: one game of size 4, so the capacity is 4.
hints: Exactly n−k pairs must be formed. Let the largest games go alone, and pair the smallest 2(n−k) values from both ends inward. The capacity is the maximum over all pair sums and the largest single game.
